note: STRICT-009 cross Windows to Linux, recorded on the host platform. The test spans the boundary: the Windows client asks the guest, through the declared transport, to create an input on the guest's own filesystem (not /mnt), runs an action over it there, and verifies the digest the guest returns against the digest the host computes locally - so any translation or line-ending step in the chain would show up as a mismatch. Storage is asserted as a measured fact: the reported filesystem type must not be drvfs and the path must not be under /mnt. Fault proof: writing the input through /mnt/c instead makes the storage assertion fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical, no FAULT markers remain. Two honest notes: the client under test is the helper in src/worker/cross_tests.zig because Jackage has no extracted cross-boundary client yet, so the fault lands there rather than in production code and will move when the client is extracted for M09; and the regression was re-recorded after the stages that precede it, which the recorder requires.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
